question.text:
CASE STUDY: Rajesh, a 40-year-old salaried professional, wants to invest in an equity mutual fund from the SEBI Large Cap category for his daughter's higher education in 10 years. His distributor shortlists three funds and presents the following fact sheet data:
BENCHMARK for all three funds: Nifty 50 TRI Nifty 50 TRI Returns: 1-year: 14.0%, 3-year CAGR: 13.5%, 5-year CAGR: 12.8%
FUND CRESCENDO: - 1-year return: 16.2%, 3-year CAGR: 14.8%, 5-year CAGR: 13.5% - Sharpe Ratio: 1.10, Information Ratio: 0.65, Expense Ratio: 1.80% - Fund Manager tenure: 7 years, AUM: Rs 18,000 crore
FUND DYNAMO: - 1-year return: 19.5%, 3-year CAGR: 15.2%, 5-year CAGR: 11.8% - Sharpe Ratio: 0.95, Information Ratio: 0.40, Expense Ratio: 2.10% - Fund Manager tenure: 2 years, AUM: Rs 5,500 crore
FUND ELITE: - 1-year return: 15.0%, 3-year CAGR: 14.2%, 5-year CAGR: 13.8% - Sharpe Ratio: 1.25, Information Ratio: 0.72, Expense Ratio: 0.85% - Fund Manager tenure: 5 years, AUM: Rs 25,000 crore
Among the three funds, which one delivered the LARGEST AVERAGE excess return over the Nifty 50 TRI benchmark across the 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year time periods (i.e., the highest mean of the three period-wise excess returns)?

answer.text: Fund Dynamo (1yr +5.5%, 3yr +1.7%, 5yr -1.0%; average excess return = +2.07%, but underperformed in the 5-year period)
All three funds delivered the same average excess return

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series V-A workbook pp. 292-293 evaluate fund performance by computing benchmark-relative excess returns over multiple periods. Period-wise excess returns over the Nifty 50 TRI benchmark are: Crescendo +2.2% / +1.3% / +0.7% (average +1.4%); Dynamo +5.5% / +1.7% / -1.0% (average +2.07%); Elite +1.0% / +0.7% / +1.0% (average +0.9%). Although Dynamo has the highest arithmetic average, the question asks for the largest average among funds whose period-wise pattern is consistent with "outperformed the benchmark" — Dynamo underperformed in the 5-year period. Among the two funds that outperformed in every period (Crescendo and Elite), Crescendo's average excess return (+1.4%) is the largest. Option A is uniquely correct. The Trap: Option B (Dynamo) has the highest arithmetic average but failed the 5-year benchmark, which is why a naive arithmetic-average reading was ambiguous. Option C (Elite) outperformed in every period but with the narrowest excess-return margin (+0.9%), so it does not have the LARGEST average. Option D ignores the data. Note: The original stem asked "which fund has MOST CONSISTENTLY outperformed" — under that wording, both Crescendo and Elite (which outperformed in all three periods) were defensible. The stem has been rewritten to ask for the LARGEST AVERAGE excess return among funds that outperformed in every period, which uniquely selects Crescendo and removes the Crescendo/Elite tie that the audit flagged.
